note: Sat 7 Nov 2026 07:02 SGT run, pre-Asia-open (markets closed for the weekend) / post-Friday-US-close. 10 of 13 items are from the last 24-48 hours (Nov 6-7): the October NFP beat, Friday's partial equity rebound, gold's Goldman-forecast-cut easing, HK tech sympathy-selling, the OCBC/DBS/UOB Q3 split, Bitcoin's selloff, and ongoing Iran/Hormuz tanker claims. No independently verified Saturday-specific escalation (Hormuz or crypto) was found as of this run -- flagged rather than assumed.

items.headline: Iran claims more tankers hit by mines near Strait of Hormuz; Trump says US is talking to Tehran via Qatar
items.summary: Iran's IRGC said two more tankers struck mines in or near the Strait of Hormuz on Friday, a day after five others were hit, keeping transits near 2-3% of pre-war levels. Trump said Washington is in contact with Tehran's representatives after a call with Qatar's Emir, even as two sources told Reuters he still intends to order renewed strikes.
items.actionable: Keep gold/silver miner exposure as the asymmetric hedge -- any resumption of US strikes on Iran would spike both oil and safe-haven metals simultaneously, favoring the levered silver/gold-miner book over cash.

items.headline: October US payrolls smash estimates at +165K, unemployment falls to 4.1%
items.summary: Nonfarm payrolls rose 165,000 in October versus a 65,000 consensus, with private payrolls up 159,000 against a 64,000 forecast. Unemployment fell to 4.1% (vs. 4.2% expected) and average hourly earnings rose 3.1% YoY, above the 2.9% forecast. CME-implied December-hike odds rose from the mid-60s/low-70s pre-print into the high-70s/~80% post-print.
items.actionable: A strong jobs beat plus hot wage growth reinforces the hawkish Fed narrative that already drove Goldman to cut its gold forecast -- expect near-term pressure on bullion even though miners have structural momentum.

items.headline: Nasdaq enters correction as AI-capex fears trigger worst selloff since April 2025 tariff shock
items.summary: The S&P 500 fell 4.36% and the Nasdaq 5.52% Thursday, with the Dow down over 1,800 points, after Texas governor-elect Gina Hinojosa's anti-data-center platform and a Democratic midterm sweep raised fears of tighter AI/data-center regulation. The VIX surged 69.7% to 28.18, its biggest jump in nearly two years.
items.actionable: The AI-regulation shock that hit US chip names is the same narrative dragging Tencent, SMIC and Xiaomi lower in Hong Kong -- HK tech is trading as a high-beta proxy on US AI-capex sentiment, not on its own fundamentals, for now.

items.headline: US stocks stage partial rebound as chip stocks bounce, but Nasdaq stays in correction
items.summary: The S&P 500 rose 0.31% and the Nasdaq 1.09% Friday as semiconductor names (Applied Materials +4.7%, AMD +11-13%) bounced, but the index remained in correction territory. For the week, the Dow fell 0.94%, the S&P 2.68% and the Nasdaq 3.37%.
items.actionable: The bounce is a relief rally within a correction, not a reversal -- don't chase HK/AI-adjacent names on this strength alone; wait for AMAT's Nov 12 earnings to confirm whether AI-capex demand is actually intact.

items.headline: Gold eases to $4,077 but posts best week in two months; Goldman slashes year-end forecast on hawkish Fed
items.summary: Spot gold fell 0.3% Friday to $4,076.91/oz but was still up 5% on the week, its strongest weekly gain in over two months. Goldman Sachs cut its end-2026 gold forecast to $4,150 from $4,650 and its 2027 forecast to $4,800 from $5,400, citing the Fed's hawkish shift; traders see December-hike odds now in the high-70s/~80%.
items.actionable: Near-term momentum in gold/silver remains intact (best week in months), but the sharply lower Goldman target signals institutional conviction is fading -- a reason to trim into strength rather than add on the levered miner book.

items.headline: China's rare-earth export-control pause set to expire Nov 10 with no formal renewal notice yet
items.summary: Beijing's temporary suspension of rare-earth export controls lapses November 10, 2026, and China has not yet published a formal notice on what follows. MP Materials and USA Rare Earth are seen as the primary beneficiaries if the pause lapses into renewed restrictions, tightening Western supply further.
items.actionable: November 10 is the single highest-impact date on the rare-earth watchlist this month -- a lapse into tighter Chinese export controls would be a direct bullish catalyst for MP, UUUU and Lynas versus Chinese processors like 6680.HK.

items.headline: MP Materials posts surprise Q3 profit as NdPr volumes nearly double and heavy rare-earth separation begins
items.summary: MP Materials reported an unexpected adjusted profit for Q3 2026, with NdPr sales volume up 94% YoY to 1,020 metric tons and materials-segment revenue up 322% YoY to $133.5 million. The company started its first heavy rare-earth separation circuits, targeting terbium and dysprosium output, and completed magnet qualification with GM.
items.actionable: MP's volume and heavy-rare-earth progress are now running ahead of its depressed share price (16-month lows into the print) -- fundamentals are improving faster than sentiment, a setup worth tracking on the watchlist.

items.headline: 'Subpoena season': Democrats target $40B of Trump-era critical-minerals deals, including MP Materials stakes
items.summary: With incoming subpoena power from January, Democratic committees are preparing investigations into roughly 160 critical-minerals deals worth about $40B, including the $8.6B in direct federal equity stakes taken in companies like MP Materials since January 2025. Lawmakers are questioning the terms and selection of these government investments.
items.actionable: Government-backed rare-earth plays now carry a real political-overhang risk heading into 2027 committee season -- size rare-earth watchlist positions with this regulatory tail risk in mind, not just the China-supply bull case.

items.headline: Hong Kong tech slides as AI concept-stock weakness spreads from Wall Street: Tencent -2%, Xiaomi/Baidu -3%, Alibaba/SMIC -4%
items.summary: Hong Kong equities closed lower Friday as AI-related large caps weakened in sympathy with the US chip selloff. Tencent fell over 2%, Xiaomi and Baidu dropped around 3%, and Alibaba and SMIC sank roughly 4% into the close.
items.actionable: The HK tech book (Tencent, SMIC, Xiaomi) is currently being priced as a direct extension of the US AI-capex trade rather than on domestic fundamentals -- any stabilization in US chip sentiment next week should flow through directly to these names.

items.headline: PBOC pledges intensified stock-market support as China equity slide defies rescue measures
items.summary: China's central bank reaffirmed support for the struggling A-share and HK markets after earlier rescue measures failed to halt the slide. The PBOC cut its share-buyback/shareholding-increase relending rate to 1% from 1.25%, made it a permanent facility, and arranged swap operations able to inject over 100 billion yuan into equities.
items.actionable: Beijing is actively trying to put a floor under China/HK tech with cheaper buyback financing, but the fact that prior measures haven't worked yet means the HK tech holdings may need more than policy support alone to stabilize -- watch for follow-through, not just announcements.

items.headline: OCBC raises 2026 guidance after beating Q3 estimates; DBS and UOB miss on weaker trading income
items.summary: OCBC posted Q3 net profit of S$2.04B (+3% YoY) and raised its 2026 loan-growth forecast to low double digits, the only one of Singapore's three banks to beat estimates. DBS and UOB both missed forecasts due to weaker trading income, and all three stocks remain down over 10% from recent peaks amid the regional selloff.
items.actionable: OCBC's guidance raise is a relative-strength signal within the SGX bank trio -- on any further regional risk-off dip, OCBC looks like the preferred name to deploy cash into versus DBS/UOB, which are showing earnings-quality cracks.

items.headline: Bitcoin falls to six-week low near $76K as tech selloff triggers $1B+ in crypto liquidations
items.summary: Bitcoin dropped to roughly $76,000 and Ether fell to about $2,230 as the US tech/AI selloff spilled into crypto. More than $1 billion in leveraged derivatives positions were liquidated in 24 hours, while US spot Bitcoin ETFs saw about $430M in net outflows and spot Ether ETFs about $100M in outflows on Nov 5.
items.actionable: Crypto is trading as a high-beta risk-asset proxy right now rather than an independent hedge -- the large cash pile is the better dry powder than crypto if more AI-capex-driven de-risking hits, since BTC/ETH are falling alongside, not against, equity risk.

items.headline: Oil holds near $90 WTI / $98 Brent as Hormuz tanker-strike claims continue, with Iran-US diplomatic contact also reported
items.summary: WTI settled near $90.34 and Brent near $97.76 Friday, both little-changed on the day after whipsawing earlier in the week on Iran/Strait-of-Hormuz tensions. Trump said the US is in contact with Tehran's representatives even as Iran's IRGC continued claiming fresh tanker-mine incidents in the Strait.
items.actionable: Oil is holding a war-risk premium without yet pricing a resumption of US strikes -- this asymmetry argues for keeping some gold/silver hedge rather than fading it on the current calm, since a strike-resumption headline could reprice both oil and metals sharply higher in a single session.
